\label{lemma-dpdga-good}
Let $(A, \text{d}, \gamma)$ and $(B, \text{d}, \gamma)$ be as in
Definition \ref{definition-divided-powers-dga}. Let $f : A \to B$
be a map of differential graded algebras compatible with divided
power structures. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $H_k(A) = 0$ for $k > 0$, and
\item $f$ is surjective.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\gamma$ induces a divided power structure on the graded
$R$-algebra $H(B)$.

statement:
Throughout, $R$ is a commutative ring and $(A,\mathrm d,\gamma)$ denotes a nonnegatively graded, strictly graded-commutative differential graded $R$-algebra equipped with a divided power structure on its positive-even part; compatibility with the differential means $\mathrm d(\gamma_n(x))=\mathrm d(x)\gamma_{n-1}(x)$ for homogeneous $x$ of positive even degree.
Let $(A, \text{d}, \gamma)$ and $(B, \text{d}, \gamma)$ be as in
the compatible divided-power DGA notion specified in the opening context. Let $f : A \to B$
be a map of differential graded algebras compatible with divided
power structures. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $H_k(A) = 0$ for $k > 0$, and
\item $f$ is surjective.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\gamma$ induces a divided power structure on the graded
$R$-algebra $H(B)$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-base-change-div}
Let $(A, \text{d}, \gamma)$ be as in
Definition \ref{definition-divided-powers-dga}.
Let $R \to R'$ be a ring map.
Then $\text{d}$ and $\gamma$ induce similar structures on
$A' = A \otimes_R R'$ such that $(A', \text{d}, \gamma)$ is as in
Definition \ref{definition-divided-powers-dga}.
stage_b_review_note: Source 1147–1155: any DP-DGA over commutative R and ring map R→R' inherits a compatible graded differential and divided powers on A⊗_R R', with no flatness assumption. The draft explicitly preserves arbitrary base change and both structures.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-uniqueness-tate-resolution}
Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Suppose that $(A, \text{d}, \gamma)$ and
$(B, \text{d}, \gamma)$ are as in
Definition \ref{definition-divided-powers-dga}.
Let $\overline{\varphi} : H_0(A) \to H_0(B)$ be an $R$-algebra map.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is a graded divided power polynomial algebra over $R$.
\item $H_k(B) = 0$ for $k > 0$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a map $\varphi : A \to B$ of differential
graded $R$-algebras compatible with divided powers
that lifts $\overline{\varphi}$.
stage_b_review_note: Pinned 1328–1342: DP-DGA A,B over R, A is a graded DP polynomial algebra, H_k(B)=0 for k>0 and R-algebra map H0(A)→H0(B); then a compatible DG-algebra LIFT A→B exists. Despite lemma title 'uniqueness', it does NOT claim uniqueness of the lift, and the draft correctly says only existence.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-divided-powers-on-tor}
Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $S$ and $T$ be commutative $R$-algebras.
Then there is a canonical structure
of a strictly graded commutative $R$-algebra with divided powers on
$$
\operatorname{Tor}_*^R(S, T).
$$
stage_b_review_note: Source 1374–1382: for commutative R and commutative R-algebras S,T, the total Tor_*^R(S,T) has a CANONICAL strictly graded-commutative R-algebra structure with divided powers. Stage A retains the canonical functorial type and all graded levels rather than only Tor_0.
